titulo.texto: The Stela of the Two Glyphs, the Original

guion_largo.texto:
Here is the piece you saw in the plaza, but this one is the original.

According to the INAH, the Stela of the Two Glyphs is the center of a museum hall. It is a monolith engraved with two calendar glyphs, probably tied to an important event in the history of Xochicalco.

One of the glyphs is a year, ten reed. The other is a day, nine reptile eye. The INAH guide says this was one of four stelae found at the site. The one you saw in the [Stela Plaza](xoc_05_plaza_estela_dos_glifos) is a replica.

Medina Romero proposes that this date corresponds to the inauguration of the Pyramid of the Feathered Serpents. It is a proposal, not a closed fact. What you can see is what is engraved: two signs that served to fix a moment.

Notice the carving. A stela is a tall stone with reliefs, made to be seen by many people. Someone decided that day deserved to remain in stone.

Compare with the replica you saw in the plaza
Think about which day of your life you would put in stone
